Definition: from G4637; an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul):-- tabernacle.
BiblicalUsage: Skenoma is the tabernacle, the body as a tent for the soul, and Peter uses it for his own approaching death. I think it meet, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance, knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle. David, long before, desired to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe my body is a tent, not a house. I hold that Peter's word frees me to live lightly in it, because the tent comes down and the building of God stands.
